name: רֹמַמְתִּי עֶזֶר
summary: Romamti-ezer son of Heman, one of David's singers, who drew the twenty-fourth and last lot (1Ch 25:4, 31). The name is the polel perfect, first person, of רוּם with עֵזֶר “help”: “I have exalted (my) help”, or “I have raised up help”. Heman's sons were given him “in the words of God, to lift up the horn (לְהָרִים קָרֶן)” (1Ch 25:5), and the polel is the psalms' word for exalting Yahweh (Psa 34:4; 30:2). It stands beside his brother's name Giddalti, “I have magnified”, and the two verbs are scripture's own pair (Isa 1:2; Psa 34:4).

evidence.note: The sons of Heman: … גִדַּלְתִּי וְרֹמַמְתִּי עֶזֶר …
“The twenty-fourth, לְרוֹמַמְתִּי עֶזֶר, his sons and his brothers, twelve.”
“All these were the sons of Heman the king's seer in the words of God, לְהָרִים קָרֶן.”
“Magnify Yahweh with me, and let us exalt (וּנְרוֹמְמָה) his name together.”
“אֲרוֹמִמְךָ, Yahweh”: the same stem, first person.
“בָּנִים גִּדַּלְתִּי וְרוֹמַמְתִּי”: the verbs of Giddalti and Romamti-ezer together.
“My help (עֶזְרִי) is from Yahweh”: the second element.

note: The second element עֵזֶר belongs to the entry ezer; the name is filed here under its verb. Whether it means “I have exalted (God as my) help” or “I have raised up help” scripture does not say. Some take the run of names at 1Ch 25:4 (Hananiah … Mahazioth) as the words of a psalm; the text does not say so.
